chunks: And Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from Abū Jaʿfar, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, who said:
I asked him about a man who becomes in a state of janabah in a garment, and he has no other than it with him, and he is unable to wash it. He said: He prays in it.

So there is no contradiction between these reports and the earlier reports, because we interpret these reports as referring to a situation in which removing the garment is not possible due to necessity. Even so, when he becomes able to wash the garment, he washes it and repeats the salat (prayer). This is indicated by what follows.

key_terms.أَعَادَ: he repeats the act, here the salat (prayer)
key_terms.ثَوْبٍ: garment or clothing worn for salat (prayer)
key_terms.ضَرُورَةٍ: a state of necessity that affects the ruling
key_terms.غَسْلِهِ: washing the garment to remove impurity
key_terms.يُجْنِبُ: becomes in a state of janabah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a person becomes junub in his only garment and cannot wash it before salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This report gives a fiqh ruling about one whose garment is affected by janabah and who has no other garment and cannot wash it. In a state of necessity, he prays in it, and the apparent conflict with other reports is resolved by restricting this ruling to necessity, while requiring repetition of the salat (prayer) after the garment can be washed.
